observed_text: One primitive cell already defines an optical zone-centre clock; a well-defined q is a phase relation across many cells. Amorphous solids retain a vibrational density of states but lose sharp ω(q) branches. There is no single nanometre cliff.
implied_text: The hardware is the crystalline lattice. The map as a spectrum is an extended-crystal object, not a 10–20 nm buffer.
description: Phonon dispersion requires an ordered grid; one cell sets an optical clock, but the spectrum is many-cell. Amorphization is loss of the map, not a thickness failure.
value_text: primitive cell + extended crystal; no nm cliff
notes: Contrast reflection’s connected-film buffer. Lattice constants in file: Si 5.43 Å; Al 4.05 Å; diamond 3.57 Å.

observed_text: Maximum phonon frequencies sit in the few-to-tens-of-THz class (Al’s spectrum ends near 10 THz; diamond’s near 40 THz). Si zone-centre Raman is 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz (1332 cm⁻¹). Acoustic clocks run from zero up to the zone-boundary frequency of that branch.
implied_text: ω_s(q) is the allowed-clock table. Nothing in the lattice oscillates as a phonon faster than the highest measured branch.
description: The lattice’s mechanical clocks are the measured branches, from acoustic zero up to a material-typical THz ceiling.
value_text: few–tens of THz (Al ~10 THz; diamond ~40 THz)
notes: value_si is Al’s ~10 THz ceiling as a representative. Optical zone-centre pins: Si 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz.

observed_text: The harmonic restoring energy of a mode is ½ħω(2n+1) (or ½ku² classically). Softening to ω→0 is loss of that restoring constraint along one coordinate.
implied_text: This is an oscillator budget, not an activation barrier that holds a directional state. Dispersion is not a latch.
description: Phonon branches are driven oscillators, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a written mechanical state.
value_text: ½ħω(2n+1) oscillator budget, not KV
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Driving above the highest lattice frequency produces no additional phonon mode. Zone-boundary / reststrahlen / neutron cutoff sits at the few-to-tens-of-THz class. q outside the first zone is an alias, not a new clock.
implied_text: Drive faster than the last branch → no additional lattice mode.
description: The allowed-clock table ends at the zone-boundary maximum; faster drive is not a phonon.
value_text: ω above last branch (Al ~10 THz; diamond ~40 THz)
notes: Physical ceiling is owned here; Debye ω_D is the continuum stand-in filed under debye-cutoff.

observed_text: A restoring branch can fall toward ω=0 as a structural transition is approached. An imaginary harmonic ω is the statement that the current lattice is mechanically unstable.
implied_text: Softening to ω→0 closes that restoring channel; a structural transition follows. This is not the first-order melting of Al or W.
description: A branch that loses its restoring frequency is a coordinate-specific grid instability, not the melting cliff.
value_text: ω → 0 (soft mode)
notes: Soft-mode trajectories are high as a class and medium for any one crystal’s T-axis. Melting owns Bragg-order loss.

observed_text: Loss of Bragg order ends the map. Melting or amorphization removes the discrete ω(q) branches. Finite lifetime / mean free path blurs a peak but does not erase the branch until the lattice itself fails.
implied_text: The clock table is carried by the crystal. Destroy the grid and the map ends.
description: Melting or amorphization erases the allowed-clock table by destroying the lattice that defined q.
value_text: melting / amorphization; Bragg order gone
notes: Primary owner of the thermal coexistence cliff is melting.

observed_text: Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering return discrete ω(q) peaks along each branch. Acoustic long-wave slopes match measured sound speeds (Al longitudinal ≈ 6.4 km s⁻¹; Si [100] longitudinal ≈ 8.4 km s⁻¹). Zone-centre optical pins include Si 15.5 THz and diamond 40 THz.
implied_text: The stable output is the measured surface ω_s(q), its long-wave speeds v_s, and its zone-centre optical frequencies, for as long as the crystal remains ordered.
description: The synchronized ion grid emits a material-typical allowed-clock map, not a single binary macro.
value_text: ω_s(q); v_s; Γ optical pins (Si 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz)
notes: Long-wave slope is also speed-of-sound. Do not invent a single dispersion cliff.

observed_text: QSA takes the measured ω(q) as data. Force-constant models that fit the curves are not promoted to node rules. The mapping does not predict which crystal will soften.
implied_text: Branch frequencies are located as the clock table but not derived from a more primitive set of node spring constants.
description: The allowed-clock map is taken, not computed from node springs. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
value_text: ω(q) taken, not derived
notes: File-level mapping is Medium: hardware scale is not a single number; binary macros belong to related lattice entries.

observed_text: The continuum slope is stable only for λ ≫ a (lattice constant or mean spacing). A vacuum has no coupled mechanical medium. A fluid has compressional couplings and no shear restoring couplings.
implied_text: Hardware is a coupled mechanical population with many nodes per wavelength, plus the relevant restoring modulus. There is no single nanometre-scale thickness cliff.
description: Sound requires a medium and the modulus that provisions the claimed branch. Vacuum has no nodes; fluids do not provision shear.
value_text: λ ≫ a; medium + modulus; no nm cliff

observed_text: Measured long-wave structure: v_s = √(C/ρ). Dry air at 20 °C, 1 atm: ≈ 343 m s⁻¹. Liquid water near 20 °C: ≈ 1480 m s⁻¹. Common steels, longitudinal: ≈ 5000–6000 m s⁻¹. Crystalline solids as a class sit in the kilometres-per-second range.
implied_text: The long-wave clock speed is the q→0 slope of the acoustic branch on the same grid phonon-dispersion maps at finite q. No single v_s is universal.
description: Sound speed is the material-typical √(C/ρ) slope, not a universal constant.
value_text: v_s = √(C/ρ); air ~343 m/s; water ~1480 m/s; steels 5–6 km/s
notes: value_si left null: the file lists class examples, not one pin. Air tracks √(γRT/M) with γ ≈ 1.4; water does not follow that gas law.

observed_text: Transit time on a path L is t = L/v_s. Relative to a human clock a laboratory path is still delayed: milliseconds in air across a room, microseconds in a metal bar of similar length. That clock is orders of magnitude slower than the zone-boundary / Debye clock of the same solid (terahertz class).
implied_text: The macroscopic acoustic clock is the transit L/v_s and the period λ/v_s, not the Debye ceiling.
description: A laboratory path is a millisecond (air) or microsecond (metal) delay; the same solid’s zone-boundary clock is THz.
value_text: t = L/v_s; ~ms in air across a room; ~µs in a metal bar
notes: Not a single material pin. Cross-cite debye-cutoff for the short-wave ceiling.

observed_text: The operating condition is a finite restoring modulus (bulk, and shear if a shear wave is claimed) plus a density. The wave is a launched collective oscillation, not a memory.
implied_text: No latched barrier. Presence of C and ρ provisions the slope; holding a sound field is not a zero-power memory.
description: Sound is a driven collective oscillation of coupled nodes, not a stored directional state.
value_text: finite C and ρ; no latch

observed_text: A vacuum has no coupled mechanical medium: v_s is undefined there, not a small number. A density so low that couplings do not form a collective wave on the path also produces no sound.
implied_text: No nodes, no wave. Vacuum is missing hardware, not a limiting speed of zero.
description: Sound dies when the coupled medium is absent. v_s is undefined in vacuum.
value_text: vacuum: v_s undefined

observed_text: Shear (transverse) sound exists in solids. It is absent as a propagating mode in liquids and gases at ordinary acoustic frequencies, where the shear modulus G = 0. Melting of a crystal is the same shear-branch collapse.
implied_text: G = 0 means the shear restoring couplings are not provisioned. The compressional branch can remain.
description: No shear modulus, no shear wave. Melting is that collapse of the solid’s shear branch.
value_text: G = 0 → no shear wave (fluids; melt)
notes: Cross-cite melting. Dissipative attenuation is a different, non-modulus cliff.

observed_text: A material-typical, frequency-independent (long-wave) pair {v_L, v_T} in a solid, or a single v_L in a fluid. Examples: air ≈ 343 m s⁻¹; water ≈ 1480 m s⁻¹; steels 5000–6000 m s⁻¹.
implied_text: The synchronized long-wavelength output of the coupled mechanical population is that material-typical slope set.
description: The machine emits a handbook v_s class, not one universal speed.
value_text: {v_L, v_T} solid; v_L fluid (air ~343 m/s; steels km/s)
notes: Same springs as elasticity, read as a slope. qa ~ 1 moves the mode onto the phonon-dispersion curve.

observed_text: A closed mapping would say why a given solid has the C it has, from node-spring rules, rather than taking handbook moduli as input. The speed measurement does not depend on closing it.
implied_text: QSA takes measured C and ρ and reads v_s = √(C/ρ). It does not derive the moduli from node springs.
description: The slope is located; the springs that set C are not derived here. Same gap as elasticity.
value_text: C, ρ taken; v_s = √(C/ρ)
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Ideal-gas air and condensed water share the Newton–Laplace form on different hardware; ideal-gas-pressure owns the wall force, not this slope.

observed_text: N atoms ⇒ 3N mechanical degrees of freedom, hence at most 3N lattice modes. That ceiling is a counting fact, independent of the Debye approximation used to locate it.
implied_text: The clock ceiling exists because the node count is finite. A macroscopic crystal still has a highest mechanical frequency.
description: Finite N is the hardware: 3N modes, no more. The Debye sphere is only a way to place that count on a linear spectrum.
value_text: 3N modes (3 per atom)
notes: A molecule or cluster has a discrete vibrational set and no continuum Debye sphere.

observed_text: Corresponding clock class, from the definition of Θ_D: a few terahertz for Pb-class Θ_D (~100 K), tens of terahertz for diamond-class Θ_D (~2000 K). Thermal occupation of the last modes requires kT ~ ħω_D = kΘ_D.
implied_text: ω_D is the clock ceiling of the ion grid under the linear-spectrum count. Below it only a T³-growing fraction of the 3N modes is in play; above it the mechanical spectrum is fully occupied.
description: The Debye clock is a few THz (Pb class) to tens of THz (diamond class), the continuum stand-in for the zone-boundary ceiling.
value_text: few THz (Pb class) to tens of THz (diamond class)
notes: Do not convert Θ_D to a single invented ω_D pin. Real ceiling is the Brillouin-zone boundary on phonon-dispersion.

observed_text: ħω_D is a spectral edge, not an activation energy that protects a memory. The operating condition is a surviving lattice with a finite number of oscillators.
implied_text: No latched barrier. Θ_D organizes occupation of the last modes; it does not hold a written state.
description: The Debye edge is a cutoff on the oscillator table, not a KV-style memory barrier.
value_text: ħω_D = kΘ_D spectral edge, not a latch
notes: Θ_D is not a melting temperature.

observed_text: Modes with ω > ω_D are simply not present in the count. No additional lattice-mode heat capacity appears once the thermal window is above the last mechanical frequency. The grid does not go transparent the way a metal does above ω_p.
implied_text: Drive or thermal weight at ω > ω_D finds no further lattice mode to occupy. The mode is absent, not evanescent.
description: Above the finite-mode ceiling there is no extra phonon channel. That is a cutoff, not a plasma-edge transmission.
value_text: ω > ω_D (mode absent)
notes: Do not identify this with reflection’s plasma-edge collapse.

observed_text: If the lattice is destroyed, the 3N crystalline modes are gone and the liquid has a different, overdamped spectrum. Lead is already classical at 300 K and still solid until T_m ≈ 600 K; diamond’s Θ_D class sits near 2000 K and the 1 atm solid does not melt.
implied_text: Melting removes the crystalline mode table. Exceeding Θ_D does not.
description: Grid destruction, not Θ_D overrun, ends the 3N crystalline clocks.
value_text: melting ends 3N modes; Θ_D ≠ T_m (Pb T_m ≈ 600 K)
notes: Cross-cite melting.

observed_text: N too small for a density of states → discrete molecular lines, not a Debye continuum. The hardware for the Debye interpolation is a 3-D lattice large enough that mode counting can be replaced by an integral up to q_D ∼ 2π/a.
implied_text: The continuum cutoff is a large-N object. Under-provisioned N is a different spectrum, not a lower Θ_D of the same machine.
description: A cluster does not run a Debye sphere. Continuum Θ_D requires a lattice large enough for the q_D integral.
value_text: N too small → discrete lines, not Debye
notes: Using one ω_D on a crystal with hard optical branches or strong anisotropy makes Θ_D a fit parameter rather than a hardware pin.

observed_text: Handbook class: Pb Θ_D ∼ 100 K; diamond Θ_D ∼ 2000 K. Room temperature (≈ 300 K) sits above the lead ceiling and far below the diamond ceiling. Low-T insulator heat capacity follows T³; high-T lattice heat capacity saturates at 3Nk (Dulong–Petit).
implied_text: A material-typical Θ_D and the two heat-capacity limits it organizes are the averaged output of a finite, synchronized mechanical population.
description: The finite-mode machine emits a Θ_D class from ~100 K (Pb) to ~2000 K (diamond), with T³ and 3Nk as the organized bounds.
value_text: Θ_D ~100 K (Pb) to ~2000 K (diamond)
notes: Any one numerical Θ_D is medium (extraction method moves the number inside the class). Metals add a separate γT term owned by electron-heat-capacity.

observed_text: Identifying the ceiling with a single spherical ω_D is an interpolation: the measured ceiling is the zone-boundary set on phonon-dispersion. QSA currently takes handbook Θ_D as the clock specification and does not derive it from a more primitive node rule.
implied_text: The 3N ceiling is tight; the Debye-sphere pin is taken, not derived.
description: Finite mode count is closed. A single spherical Θ_D is an interpolation over the real zone boundary.
value_text: Θ_D taken; sphere vs zone boundary
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Gap is the sphere versus the real zone boundary, not the existence of a cutoff.

observed_text: A crystalline grid large enough to produce Bragg peaks and a macroscopic shear modulus. A few-atom cluster has no bulk T_m; a glass has no Bragg grid. Glasses and amorphous solids do not have this T_m cliff; their softening is a viscosity / timescale crossover.
implied_text: The sharp hardware is the ordered lattice itself, not a universal millimetre envelope.
description: Melting is a property of a Bragg-ordered, shear-carrying grid. Clusters and glasses are different machines.
value_text: Bragg grid + shear; no universal mm envelope

observed_text: Thermal vibration of the ions has a spectral ceiling at the Debye / zone-boundary clock. Melting is not that clock being exceeded. Nucleation and front propagation set the laboratory time to complete the conversion and are not a single material pin.
implied_text: The conversion clock is nucleation and front motion, unpinned. Exceeding Θ_D is not melting.
description: Melting is loss of restoring couplings, not Debye-clock overrun. No single laboratory conversion time is extracted.
value_text: nucleation / front; not Θ_D overrun
notes: Pb: Θ_D ∼ 100 K, T_m ≈ 600 K. Diamond Θ_D class ∼ 2000 K; 1 atm solid sublimes rather than a tungsten-style melt.

observed_text: Measured 1 atm melting points: ice T_m = 273.15 K; aluminum T_m = 933 K; tungsten T_m = 3695 K. These are empirical failure temperatures of the respective grids. The latent heat is the energy that must be supplied at coexistence. There is no simple anisotropy-style barrier KV from which T_m is computed in this mapping.
implied_text: The load-bearing threshold is the measured T_m: kT in the presence of the crystal’s cohesion is then sufficient to unbind the ordered grid.
description: T_m is the measured thermal gate of the grid, not a derived KV-style barrier.
notes: value_si left null: three empirical pins, not one universal T_m. First-order for these three: latent heat, volume jump, two-phase plateau.

observed_text: T → T_m at the ambient pressure → loss of Bragg order, loss of static shear, conversion to a fluid that carries only compressional sound. Superheating can temporarily overshoot T_m; the equilibrium collapse point remains the measured coexistence temperature.
implied_text: Thermal unbinding of the ordered grid at the measured coexistence T_m. Shear sound and static shear die with the solid.
description: The grid fails at T_m: Bragg gone, G → 0, only compressional sound remains.
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound (no shear in the melt) and elasticity (G → 0).

observed_text: The grid can also be destroyed below T_m by large plastic strain, radiation amorphization, or dissolution.
implied_text: Those are lattice-destruction routes, not the thermal coexistence cliff.
description: Plastic strain, radiation, or dissolution can erase the grid without reaching T_m.
value_text: plastic strain / radiation amorphization / dissolution
notes: Latch entries may list lattice destruction as a secondary failure; they own the latch, this file owns the grid.

observed_text: Below T_m, a solid with Bragg order and a shear modulus. At T_m, a first-order conversion whose temperature is a material constant at given pressure. Above T_m, a fluid without that grid.
implied_text: The stable product is the coexistence temperature itself plus the solid/fluid sides of the cliff.
description: The machine’s output is an ordered shear-carrying solid below T_m and a first-order conversion at the measured pin.
value_text: T_m(P) (ice 273.15 K; Al 933 K; W 3695 K at 1 atm)
notes: Clapeyron organizes dT_m/dP = ΔV/ΔS; ice ΔV < 0. It does not give T_m(P=0).

observed_text: Lindemann criterion (conventional, not a derivation): the crystal is near melting when √⟨u²⟩/a ∼ 0.1–0.15. The number correlates with T_m across many solids; it does not predict T_m from node rules, and the prefactor is structure-dependent.
implied_text: QSA takes measured T_m as the empirical threshold. Lindemann is a displacement consistency check, not a derived barrier.
description: The mapping does not close on why ice, Al, and W fail at those temperatures. Lindemann is not a node-level derivation of T_m.
value_text: √⟨u²⟩/a ∼ 0.1–0.15 near T_m (criterion)
notes: File-level mapping is Medium while T_m data are High. Cohesive well depth, coordination, and anharmonicity (thermal-expansion) enter and are not yet primitive node specifications. Soft-mode melting belongs with phonon-dispersion. value_si is the 0.1–0.15 window midpoint.

observed_text: A lattice that supports propagating acoustic modes, plus a mean free path. In the Casimir limit the spatial buffer is the specimen: ℓ saturates at the specimen size and shrinking L lowers κ at low T. In a glass the effective ℓ is already microscopic and the crystal-style peak never forms.
implied_text: Hardware is the phonon-carrying grid plus the scattering length ℓ. At low T the buffer is the sample itself.
description: Phonon κ requires a propagating lattice and an ℓ. Casimir makes the specimen the spatial buffer; a glass never provisions the crystal peak.
value_text: ℓ plus lattice; Casimir ℓ ~ L_sample
notes: A metal’s phonon channel is present but is not the macroscopic κ this entry maps.

observed_text: Carrier speed v is the long-wave acoustic slope. The transport clock is the scattering time τ = ℓ/v: boundary-limited and long at low T, umklapp-limited and short at high T. Zone-boundary / Debye periods remain the underlying oscillator clocks.
implied_text: Transport latency is ℓ/v, not the Debye period. No single τ is extracted.
description: The heat-current clock is the scattering time set by ℓ. Oscillator clocks stay with debye-cutoff.
value_text: τ = ℓ/v (unpinned)
notes: v owned by speed-of-sound; C(T) by debye-cutoff; this file owns ℓ.

observed_text: No latched barrier. Umklapp is a kinematic threshold in the phonon population (enough large-q modes occupied) rather than an activation barrier that stores a state. T → 0 starves C; T → T_m removes the grid.
implied_text: The transport spec has occupation and grid conditions, not a memory barrier.
description: Phonon heat current is not a latch. Umklapp is kinematic; T → 0 or melting starve the channel.
value_text: umklapp kinematic; C→0 as T→0; grid to T_m

observed_text: Umklapp, defects, isotopes, or amorphization collapse ℓ and κ falls. At high T, C has saturated and ℓ continues to drop, so κ falls (often roughly as 1/T in simple crystals). Umklapp requires the reciprocal lattice; normal processes do not by themselves degrade a heat current in the Peierls accounting.
implied_text: ℓ is the load-bearing transport resource. Shorten it and the heat current dies even while the modes still exist.
description: The transport spec fails when the mean free path collapses — umklapp at high T, or defects / glass.
value_text: ℓ collapse (umklapp / defects / glass); κ often ~1/T at high T
notes: No reciprocal lattice, no umklapp (phonon-dispersion owns the zone). Same anharmonicity thermal-expansion names.

observed_text: Specimen size below the intrinsic ℓ (Casimir) → κ set by L, not by bulk scattering. Low T, clean crystal: ℓ saturates at the specimen size, C ∝ T³, so κ ∝ T³.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning of the path makes the sample the buffer. That is a size failure of the bulk-κ spec.
description: When L < intrinsic ℓ, the heat current is boundary-limited and κ tracks the specimen, not bulk umklapp.
value_text: L ≲ ℓ (Casimir); κ ∝ T³ at low T
notes: Any one peak temperature or residual ℓ is sample-dependent (medium).

observed_text: This channel collapses if the grid is destroyed (melting) or if T → 0 (C → 0). It is not the electronic Wiedemann–Franz channel.
implied_text: Destroy the grid or starve C and this phonon κ is gone. Measuring a metal and attributing κ to phonons is the wrong machine.
description: Melting or T → 0 ends the phonon heat current. Electronic κ is a different population.
value_text: T → T_m or T → 0; not Wiedemann–Franz
notes: Cross-cite melting and electron-heat-capacity.

observed_text: Room-temperature class: diamond κ ∼ 10³ W m⁻¹ K⁻¹; typical oxide glasses κ ∼ 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. A good crystal’s κ is small at the lowest T, rises, peaks (often tens of kelvin), and then falls.
implied_text: A material- and size-dependent κ(T) with the crystal peak-and-fall shape, produced by a synchronized phonon population limited by ℓ.
description: The transport machine emits a crystal κ(T) peak and a diamond-vs-glass class of about 10³ vs 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
value_text: diamond ~10³ W m⁻¹ K⁻¹; oxide glasses ~1; crystal peak-and-fall
notes: Kinetic structure κ = (1/3) C v ℓ is descriptive data; the 1/3 is a kinetic average, not a derived node rule.

observed_text: The mapping takes the kinetic formula and the Peierls umklapp distinction as descriptive data. It does not yet extract a particular ℓ(T) from node-level anharmonicity.
implied_text: The failing resource (ℓ) is identified; its value is not derived from node rules.
description: QSA names ℓ as the transport buffer but does not compute ℓ(T) from anharmonicity. Same unfinished anharmonicity as thermal-expansion.
value_text: κ = (1/3) C v ℓ taken; ℓ(T) underived
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Electronic thermal conductivity belongs with the electron population.

observed_text: A mechanically coupled grid (or, for K only, a fluid density field). The linear modulus is already a bulk average of the same springs whose long-wave slope is v_s. There is no single nanometre cliff for E itself. The yield envelope requires a mesoscale population of dislocations, grain boundaries, or cracks.
implied_text: Hookean E is a grid average. Yield is a different, defect-structure buffer on the same crystal.
description: Small-strain stiffness lives on the ion grid; plasticity lives on a mesoscale defect population.
value_text: coupled grid for E; mesoscale defects for yield
notes: Elastomers are entropy-elastic and not this ion-grid machine.

observed_text: Hooke’s law holds only at small strain. In ordinary metals the reversible window is a strain of order 10⁻³ or less.
implied_text: The linear restoring output is specified only inside that small-strain window.
description: Ordinary metals stay Hookean only to strains of order 10⁻³ or less.
value_text: strain ≲ 10⁻³ (ordinary metals)
notes: Polymers and elastomers are a different, large-strain machine.

observed_text: Reversible elastic response tracks the acoustic / Debye clocks of the grid: microscopic restoration is fast compared with ordinary mechanical tests. Plastic flow is slower and rate-dependent.
implied_text: The Hookean clock is the acoustic / Debye table. Plastic latency belongs to defect motion, not to the harmonic spring.
description: Microscopic restoration is acoustic-fast; yield latency is a different, slower defect clock.
value_text: acoustic / Debye restore; plastic slower
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound and debye-cutoff. No invented period.

observed_text: Small-strain elasticity is a restoring well, not a latch: stored energy ½ C ε² is returned on unload. Yield is a threshold on that well’s useful range. In crystals the microscopic barrier being crossed is a dislocation Peierls / pinning barrier — measured as a yield stress, not yet specified here as a KV-style node number.
implied_text: The Hookean machine stores and returns ½ C ε². It is not a directional memory. Yield is the well’s useful-range cliff, not a latch write.
description: Elastic energy is returned on unload. Yield is a range threshold, not a remanence barrier.
value_text: ½ C ε² returned; yield ≠ KV

observed_text: Mild steels yield at hundreds of MPa, far below E. Above a yield stress the solid flows plastically or fractures and does not recover. The conventional ideal-strength estimate E/10 sits one to two orders of magnitude above real metallic yield.
implied_text: Load above yield or fracture toughness ends the linear emergent output. Real yield is a mesoscale cliff, not E/10.
description: Plastic set or fracture is the load-bearing failure of the Hookean machine. Real metallic yield is far below the ideal bond-breaking estimate.
value_text: mild steel yield: hundreds of MPa (≪ E; ≪ E/10)
notes: A particular alloy’s yield is processing-dependent. E/10 is a conventional estimate, not a measured cliff. resource is energy density (Pa = J/m³).

observed_text: Static shear modulus G → 0 on melting. The liquid keeps a bulk modulus. No shear couplings (fluid, vacuum) → no static shear modulus.
implied_text: The solid elastic machine dies with the grid. Compression can remain as a fluid K.
description: Melting (or any medium without shear couplings) removes static G. K can survive.
value_text: G → 0 at T_m; fluid / vacuum: no static shear
notes: Cross-cite melting and speed-of-sound. Amplitude large enough to leave the Hooke window is nonlinear elasticity until yield.

observed_text: Handbook class, room temperature: steels E ≈ 200 GPa; aluminum E ≈ 70 GPa; diamond E ∼ 10³ GPa. Shear and bulk moduli are the same class of measured stiffnesses. Water’s bulk modulus is the C that gives v_s ≈ 1480 m s⁻¹ at ρ ≈ 10³ kg m⁻³.
implied_text: Handbook moduli {E, G, K} are the synchronized small-amplitude restoring output of the coupled nodes, together with a material- and history-dependent yield / fracture envelope.
description: The ion grid emits a GPa-class stiffness set. The same C is the slope v = √(C/ρ).
value_text: steels E ≈ 200 GPa; Al ≈ 70 GPa; diamond ∼ 10³ GPa
notes: value_si is the steel E pin as a representative of the class. Harmonic C is independent of strain and volume to first order; real C(T) needs thermal-expansion.

observed_text: The conventional ideal-strength estimate E/10 sits one to two orders of magnitude above real metallic yield. That gap is the mesoscale dislocation / microstructure step — the mechanical analogue of coercivity versus anisotropy field.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer / barrier specification for dislocation nucleation and pinning. The Hookean output does not depend on closing it.
description: Yield / fracture is identified as a mesoscale envelope and is not reduced to a node-level barrier. Same unfinished step as magnet coercivity.
value_text: real yield ≪ E/10; mesoscale
notes: Cross-cite ferromagnetic-hysteresis and permanent-magnet-latch (Hc ≪ Ha). File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: Linear piezoelectricity requires a lattice without an inversion center. Twenty of the 32 crystal classes meet that condition. A centrosymmetric crystal of any size does not provision the linear coupling. A crystalline or poled ceramic lattice must be large enough for a macroscopic stress and a macroscopic polarization to be defined.
implied_text: The hardware is an inversion-free grid. Size does not create d_ij if inversion is present. Polar memory of a poled ferroelectric is owned by ferroelectric-remanence.
description: The linear strain–polarization machine is provisioned only by a non-centrosymmetric lattice (20 of 32 classes).
value_text: 20 of 32 classes inversion-free; d_ij = 0 with inversion
notes: Centrosymmetric crystals may still show quadratic electrostriction, which is not this entry.

observed_text: The mechanical side tracks the acoustic clocks of elasticity / speed-of-sound (transit across the plate). The electrical side tracks the dielectric response of the bound-charge population. Laboratory piezo devices are usually limited by the plate resonance, not by an atomic period.
implied_text: Device latency is the acoustic transit / plate resonance, not an atomic piezo clock.
description: No single atomic piezo period is extracted. Laboratory clocks sit at the plate resonance.
value_text: plate resonance / acoustic transit (unpinned)
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound and refraction-dielectric.

observed_text: The existence gate is inversion-free lattice symmetry, not an energy barrier. Quartz is not a ferroelectric latch; its coupling tracks the non-centrosymmetric lattice, not a switchable remnant polarization. Coercive field writes the polar latch; it is not the piezo coupling itself.
implied_text: Linear piezo is a symmetry-gated coupling, not a memory. Ferroelectric remnant P is a different machine sharing some crystals.
description: No piezo latch. The gate is inversion-free symmetry; quartz does not die with a remnant-P write.
value_text: inversion-free gate; not a KV / P_r latch
notes: Ferroelectric T_C is an additional thermal threshold on the large polar d_ij. Cross-cite ferroelectric-remanence.

observed_text: Centrosymmetric crystals have d_ij = 0 for the linear effect (Si, NaCl, most metals; or a phase that restored inversion).
implied_text: If inversion is a symmetry, the linear output is forbidden, independent of field strength short of breakdown.
description: Inversion present → d_ij = 0. As sharp a hardware condition as the plasma-frequency clock on reflection.
value_text: inversion present ⇒ d_ij = 0
notes: Dielectric breakdown at high E is a different cliff (dielectric-breakdown).

observed_text: The large polar d_ij of PZT / BaTiO3 vanishes with the polar phase above T_C (BaTiO3 T_C ≈ 393 K; PZT T_C is composition-dependent, typically a few hundred °C). Quartz α–β at 573 °C changes the coefficients; β-quartz remains non-centrosymmetric. Quartz does not die at a ferroelectric T_C.
implied_text: PZT fails as a large piezo at ferroelectric T_C even while a solid remains. Quartz fails only by losing the non-centrosymmetric grid.
description: Ferroelectric piezo has a T_C collapse of the large d_ij. Quartz does not share that cliff.
value_text: T > T_C (BaTiO3 ≈ 393 K; PZT few hundred °C)
notes: value_si is BaTiO3 T_C. Two collapse routes must not be collapsed into one sentence. Remnant P owned by ferroelectric-remanence.

observed_text: Lattice destruction (melting) removes the coupling with the grid. Cracking of the grid ends the coupling. Drive out of the linear window produces harmonics and, in ferroelectrics, depoling.
implied_text: No inversion-free solid, no linear d_ij. Shock-depoling or cracking is lattice damage, not a second copy of melting.
description: Melting or cracking destroys the strain–polarization hardware with the lattice.
value_text: melting / cracking; linear-window / depoling
notes: Cross-cite melting. Mechanical-lattice damage on the latch is not restated as a second melting.

observed_text: Handbook coupling class: quartz and AlN sit in the single-digit to ~10 pC N⁻¹ class (quartz d_11 ≈ 2.3 pC N⁻¹ is a standard cut number); PZT ceramics sit in the 10² pC N⁻¹ class.
implied_text: A linear, reversible strain ↔ polarization conversion with a material-typical d_ij, present only while the inversion-free (and, if ferroelectric, polar) lattice holds.
description: The coupling output is a pC/N-class d_ij: quartz ~2, PZT ~10², only inside the symmetry / polar envelope.
value_text: quartz d_11 ≈ 2.3 pC N⁻¹; AlN ~1–10; PZT 10² class
notes: value_si is the quartz d_11 pin. A particular ceramic’s d_33 is medium (process- and composition-dependent). Specific commercial PZT grades are not a single pin.

observed_text: The mapping takes handbook d_ij as the coupling strength. QSA does not yet derive why quartz is ~2 pC N⁻¹ and PZT is 10² class from node rules.
implied_text: The symmetry gate and T_C collapse are located; the magnitude of d is taken, not computed.
description: Coupling magnitude is a handbook input. That is the principal reason the mapping is medium rather than high.
value_text: d_ij taken (quartz ~2 vs PZT 10² class)
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Polar latch is a different machine sharing the same crystal.

observed_text: An ordered magnetic population sitting in a deformable lattice, large enough for a macroscopic ΔL and a macroscopic M. A paramagnetic crystal has the lattice and not the ordered moment. A liquid magnet (if any) has no static shear grid to register a linear λ_s of this kind.
implied_text: Hardware is ordered M plus a strain-carrying grid. Grain-scale latching of M is owned by permanent-magnet-latch / superparamagnetism; this file owns the strain that follows M.
description: Magnetostriction needs both an ordered moment and a deformable lattice. Either alone is not this machine.
value_text: ordered M + deformable lattice
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. Centrosymmetric iron is magnetostrictive and not piezoelectric.

observed_text: Magnetic side: precession / domain-wall clocks of the magnet entries. Mechanical side: acoustic transit of elasticity. Laboratory λ(H) loops are limited by the field sweep and by eddy currents / walls, not by the 28 GHz/T carrier.
implied_text: The length-change clock is the magnet’s write / wall motion plus acoustic transit, not the Larmor carrier.
description: No separate magnetostrictive period is extracted. Lab loops are sweep- and wall-limited.
value_text: sweep / walls / eddy; not 28 GHz/T
notes: The 28 GHz/T Larmor carrier is owned by permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: No separate magnetostrictive latch. The thresholds are the host magnet’s: T_C, the anisotropy / coercivity write field, and the mechanical integrity of the grid. Magnetoelastic energy is an extra term in the anisotropy budget; it can raise or lower the latch barrier but is not the barrier’s origin in NdFeB-class K_1.
implied_text: This file must not re-specify the magnet. Strain is locked to M; the barrier that holds M is the latch’s.
description: Magnetostriction is a coupling, not a latch. T_C, KV, and coercivity stay with permanent-magnet-latch.
value_text: host T_C / coercivity / grid; not a second K_1
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. Inverse (Villari) stress–M is a write / read channel on that latch.

observed_text: λ → 0 as T → T_C⁻ of the ordered magnet. Fe T_C ≈ 1043 K. Ni and Terfenol-D fail at their own, lower, Curie points. This is the same thermal cliff that erases net M on permanent-magnet-latch.
implied_text: T > T_C → ordered moment gone → λ = 0. This file owns the length change, not the latch.
description: Magnetostriction dies at the host Curie point with the ordered moment.
value_text: T > T_C (Fe ≈ 1043 K; Ni / Terfenol-D lower)
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch, which owns remanence, T_C, and KV. value_si is Fe T_C as the file’s numerical pin.

observed_text: Plastic deformation, cracking, or melting removes the lattice that carries ΔL. Severe shock can also scramble the latch via this coupling without a bulk melt.
implied_text: No grid, no λ. The mechanical failure path named on permanent-magnet-latch is this coupling plus ordinary plasticity.
description: Lattice damage ends ΔL and can write error into M without reaching T_C.
value_text: plastic / cracked / melted / shock
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch (lattice-shock row): the latch entry owns remanence erasure; this file owns the strain channel. Cross-cite melting for bulk grid loss.

observed_text: λ follows M(H) and saturates once the domain population is aligned. A small field on a hard magnet produces little λ until the write field is reached. Vanishing spin–lattice coupling (λ_s → 0) leaves the moment and does not change the length.
implied_text: Macroscopic ΔL is small if M is not aligned, even when λ_s is finite. Alignment is a domain / coercivity condition, not a second coupling.
description: Unaligned domains or a hard magnet below coercivity hide λ_s. λ_s → 0 is a different, material failure.
value_text: M not aligned (below write field); or λ_s → 0
notes: Cross-cite magnetic-domains and ferromagnetic-hysteresis.

observed_text: Saturation magnetostriction λ_s = ΔL/L: Ni λ_s ∼ 10⁻⁵ (negative); Fe polycrystalline average 10⁻⁵ class or smaller; Terfenol-D (Tb–Dy–Fe) λ_s in the 10⁻³ class.
implied_text: A saturation strain λ_s locked to the aligned moment, plus the inverse stress–M channel, while the ordered magnet and the lattice both remain.
description: The strain output is a material-typical λ_s class from ~10⁻⁵ (Ni) to ~10⁻³ (Terfenol-D), locked to aligned M.
value_text: Ni ~10⁻⁵ (negative); Terfenol-D ~10⁻³
notes: Volume magnetostriction is a separate, usually smaller, channel and is the Invar cancellation term owned by thermal-expansion. A particular polycrystal’s λ_s is medium (texture- and stress-dependent).

observed_text: Why λ_s spans 10⁻⁵ (Ni) to 10⁻³ (Terfenol-D) is not extracted from a node rule here. Crystal-field and magnetoelastic coefficients are taken as data, the same way d_33 is taken as data on piezoelectricity.
implied_text: The T_C and lattice-destruction collapses are located; λ_s is a handbook coupling.
description: Coupling magnitude is taken, not derived from a stated node-level spring. Mapping confidence is therefore medium.
value_text: λ_s taken (10⁻⁵ vs 10⁻³ class)
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch: do not re-specify remanence, T_C, or KV here.

observed_text: A mechanically coupled lattice whose wells are not purely quadratic, large enough for a macroscopic length to be defined. If the restoring wells are purely quadratic, ⟨x⟩ is independent of T and α = 0. The harmonic grid that already produces speed-of-sound, elasticity, and debye-cutoff is not sufficient.
implied_text: Expansion is the anharmonic correction to the same ion-grid hardware. Harmonic springs provision moduli and a long-wave slope and still give α = 0.
description: The extra hardware is anharmonicity (γ ≠ 0), not a fourth reading of the harmonic springs.
value_text: γ ≠ 0 anharmonic wells; harmonic grid insufficient
notes: Invar adds a magnetic volume channel on top of the lattice term (magnetostriction).

observed_text: There is no separate expansion clock. The lattice clocks are the phonon spectrum; α(T) is the thermal occupation of those modes acting through γ. The laboratory length change follows the thermal equilibration time of the specimen, not an atomic period.
implied_text: α is an occupation readout of the existing phonon table, delayed only by specimen thermalization.
description: No dedicated expansion period is extracted. Laboratory ΔL follows thermal equilibration.
value_text: no separate clock; follows thermal equilibration
notes: Cross-cite phonon-dispersion and thermal-equilibrium-temperature.

observed_text: No latched barrier and no single threshold number. The operating condition is γ ≠ 0 (anharmonic wells) plus a finite T. The stated collapse is the harmonic limit γ → 0, a condition on the wells rather than a measured T or E. There is no measured γ_c at which expansion turns on.
implied_text: Expansion is not a gated latch. γ of order one for many solids is a descriptive class, not a cliff.
description: No activation barrier and no γ_c. Anharmonic wells plus finite T are the operating condition.
value_text: γ of order one; no γ_c
notes: γ → 0 is the harmonic-limit statement. value_si is the order-one class, not a pin.

observed_text: A purely harmonic spring lattice would not expand — its mean bond length is independent of amplitude. γ → 0 (purely harmonic springs) → α = 0. This is the taxonomy collapse. It is a limiting condition, not a laboratory switch one flips on a given metal.
implied_text: Remove anharmonicity and the length-change machine disappears, even though moduli, sound speed, and the 3N mode count remain.
description: The harmonic lattice does not expand. That is the named collapse of this effect.
value_text: γ → 0 ⇒ α = 0 (harmonic limit)
notes: Umklapp in thermal-conductivity-phonon draws on the same anharmonicity; the two entries should not assign contradictory γ.

observed_text: α → 0 as T → 0, tracking the vanishing of the lattice heat capacity. High temperature: α continues until the grid fails (melting). There is no single α-defined collapse temperature analogous to T_m or T_C.
implied_text: Starve C_V and expansion stops even if γ is finite. Melting ends the solid’s α spec; it is not an α cliff.
description: Low T kills α with the heat capacity. Melting ends the solid; α itself has no T_C-style pin.
value_text: T → 0 ⇒ α → 0; no α-defined T_c
notes: Cross-cite debye-cutoff (C_V) and melting (high-T end of the same wells).

observed_text: Invar (Fe–Ni near the 36 wt% Ni composition): α near zero around room temperature, not because the lattice has become harmonic, but because a magnetic / volume-magnetostriction channel cancels the ordinary anharmonic term.
implied_text: α ≈ 0 without harmonic wells. That is not the harmonic-limit collapse.
description: Invar’s near-zero α is a two-channel cancellation, not γ = 0.
value_text: Invar α ≈ 0 (cancellation, not harmonic)
notes: Cross-cite magnetostriction (volume channel). Composition 36 wt% Ni is in the file.

observed_text: Metals as a class: α ∼ 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ near room temperature (handbook examples in that window: Al ∼ 2×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, Fe ∼ 1×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹).
implied_text: A small, material-typical α(T) as the averaged length change of an anharmonic, thermally occupied grid.
description: The expansion machine emits a 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ metal class, not a universal α.
notes: value_si left null: class envelope, not one pin. A particular alloy’s α(T) is medium.

observed_text: Anharmonicity is the stated condition and not a single hardware number. There is no measured γ_c at which expansion turns on. QSA does not derive the 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ class from node-well shapes.
implied_text: The resource (anharmonicity) is named; its strength is taken as data. Invar shows that α ≈ 0 can also be a cancellation, which must not be misread as γ = 0.
description: Expansion is located as the anharmonic correction, but that resource is not pinned to one measured hardware number the way ω_p or T_m is.
value_text: α class taken; no γ_c
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Quasi-harmonic ω(q) shifts organize data and do not supply a single how-anharmonic number.
